e.etymology: A combination of Anna, from Hebrew for grace, and Lee, from Old English for meadow or clearing.
A modern American combination of Ray or Rae with the popular -lynn ending.

e.meaning: name of the Roman queen of the gods
e.etymology: From Latin Iuno, the Roman goddess of marriage and queen of the gods, wife of Jupiter. The root is uncertain; one theory links it to a word for youth. The month of June is named for her.
namesakes: Juno MacGuff (pregnant teen played by Elliot Page in the 2007 film Juno)
Juno Temple (actress in Ted Lasso)

assoc.t: title teen of the 2007 film Juno
Roman queen of the gods, wife of Jupiter
Juno Beach, a D-Day landing beach in Normandy
NASA spacecraft orbiting Jupiter

e.etymology: A French spelling of Margot, the pet form of Marguerite (Margaret), from Greek margarites, pearl. The -aux spelling matches the Bordeaux wine village of Margaux.
namesakes: Margaux Hemingway (1970s model and actress, granddaughter of Ernest Hemingway)

assoc.t: Bordeaux wine village and its Chateau Margaux

e.note: The silent x trips people up; expect misspellings and the occasional MAR-gawks.

e.etymology: A recent American coinage that puts a Z on the sound of Jaylen and Kaylen, in the same family as Zayden.
The Greek spelling of Cassandra, the Trojan princess whose true prophecies no one believed. The roots are unclear; the second part is probably aner, man.
namesakes: Cassandra of Troy (prophetess of Greek myth whom no one believed)
Kassandra (heroine of the video game Assassin's Creed Odyssey)

assoc.t: a Cassandra: someone whose true warnings go unheeded
Kassandra, heroine of Assassin's Creed Odyssey

e.etymology: A spelling of Liana, which began as a short form of names ending in -liana such as Juliana and Liliana. It can also be read as Lee plus Anna.
From Greek Gaia, the Earth personified as the first goddess and mother of the Titans, from gaia, earth. It is a popular girls' name in Italy.

assoc.t: Greek goddess who personifies the Earth
Gaia hypothesis of Earth as one living system
spirit of the Earth in Captain Planet

e.etymology: A modern American combination of the word name Ember with the -lyn ending, in the pattern of Emmalyn and Everlyn.
A spelling of Colby, an English surname from villages named in Old Norse for the farm (by) of a man called Koli.
From Laramie, Wyoming, and the Laramie River, named for the French-Canadian fur trapper Jacques La Ramee, who died in the area around 1821.

assoc.t: city in Wyoming, home of the University of Wyoming
The Laramie Project, play about Matthew Shepard's murder
Laramie, a barrel racer on TV's Yellowstone
Laramie, 1959-63 TV western
Laramie, upscale trim level of Ram pickup trucks

e.etymology: From Hebrew Yitro, from a root meaning abundance or excellence. In Exodus, Jethro is the priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses.
namesakes: Jethro Bodine (dim-witted nephew on The Beverly Hillbillies)
Leroy Jethro Gibbs (lead agent on NCIS)
Jethro Tull (18th-century farming inventor and the rock band named for him)

assoc.t: Jethro Bodine of The Beverly Hillbillies

e.note: Long a stock hillbilly name in American humor, thanks to The Beverly Hillbillies.

e.etymology: First used by Shakespeare in Cymbeline, apparently a misprint of Innogen, a name from Gaelic inghean, girl or maiden.
namesakes: Imogen Heap (singer and producer of Hide and Seek)
Imogen Poots (actress)

e.etymology: A recent American coinage in the surname style of Henley and Finley. It is close to Wrenley and to Renly, a character in Game of Thrones.
Known from Sosuke Aizen, the villain of the Japanese manga and anime Bleach, where it is a surname. In the US it also fits the sound of Aiden and Zen.

assoc.t: Sosuke Aizen, villain of the anime Bleach

e.etymology: From Greek myth, where Elara was a mortal princess loved by Zeus and mother of the giant Tityos. A moon of Jupiter is named for her. The meaning of the Greek name is not known.

assoc.t: moon of Jupiter

e.meaning: of Marius; later taken as devoted to Mary
e.etymology: From Latin Marianus, a derivative of the Roman family name Marius, itself linked to the war god Mars. Christians came to read it as a masculine form of Maria, and several saints bore it.
namesakes: Mariano Rivera (Yankees Hall of Fame closer)

e.etymology: A modern Indian name usually traced to Sanskrit arna, wave or flowing water, and often described as a name of the goddess Lakshmi.
From the Turkish word evren, the universe or cosmos. It is given to both boys and girls in Turkey.
A modern Indian girls' name, popular in Bengali and Hindi-speaking families and in the Indian diaspora.
From the English place name and surname, simply oak plus land. Most Americans know it as the California city, named for its oak groves.

assoc.t: city in California on San Francisco Bay

e.etymology: The day of the week, from Old English sunnandaeg, day of the sun. It is a long-standing boys' name in Nigeria for a child born on Sunday and a recent girls' name in the US.
namesakes: Sunday Rose Kidman Urban (daughter of Nicole Kidman and Keith Urban)

assoc.t: the day of the week

e.etymology: The Spanish form of Mireille, a name the Provencal poet Frederic Mistral created for the heroine of his 1859 poem Mireio, probably from Occitan mirar, to admire.
The Spanish form of Benedict, from Late Latin Benedictus, blessed. It spread with devotion to Saint Benedict, founder of Western monasticism.
namesakes: Bad Bunny (Puerto Rican superstar, born Benito Martinez Ocasio)
Benito Mussolini (fascist dictator of Italy)
Benito Juarez (19th-century president of Mexico)

assoc.t: Benito Mussolini, Italy's fascist dictator

e.note: Many older Americans still link it to Mussolini; Bad Bunny, born Benito, has given it a newer association.

e.etymology: An old English pet form of Sarah, Hebrew for princess, with the r softened to l as in Molly from Mary. It has long been used as a name in its own right.
namesakes: Sally Field (Oscar-winning actress)
Sally Ride (first American woman in space)
Sally Brown (Charlie Brown's little sister in Peanuts)

assoc.t: Sally Beauty, beauty supply store chain
Sally, the rag doll in The Nightmare Before Christmas
Sally Carrera, the Porsche in Pixar's Cars
Sally Hansen nail polish and nail care

e.etymology: The English word used as a given name, a modern virtue name in the line of Justice and Wisdom.
In the US it rose with Kanan Stark, the character in Power and its prequel Raising Kanan. As an older name it is a form of Kenan or Kanaan, the Arabic and Turkic name for Canaan.

assoc.t: Kanan Stark of Power and Raising Kanan
Jedi Kanan Jarrus in Star Wars Rebels

e.etymology: A South Slavic form of Daniel, from Hebrew Daniyyel, God is my judge. It passed into Italian and from there into Spanish and Portuguese.
From Sanskrit dhruva, fixed or immovable. In Hindu tradition the boy Dhruva's unshakable devotion was rewarded by Vishnu, who made him the pole star.
The everyday short form of Michael, from Hebrew Mikha'el, who is like God? It has also long been given as a full name, peaking in the US around 1960.
namesakes: Mike Tyson (heavyweight boxing champion)
Mike Pence (48th US vice president)
Mike Wazowski (one-eyed monster in Monsters, Inc.)

assoc.t: short for microphone, as in open mike
Mike's Hard Lemonade
Jersey Mike's Subs
Mike and Ike chewy candy

e.etymology: A modern American name, most likely an elaboration of David or Davon with the -ion ending. It matches a rare French surname from a pet form of David, but is not a given name in France.

e.meaning: lane, narrow road; also wave in Estonian
e.etymology: In the US, a spelling of Lane, the English surname for someone who lived by a lane, and a short form of Elaine. Laine is also an Estonian girls' name meaning wave and a common Finnish surname.
